why: Abroad on metered roaming, iOS reclaims the inactive 38 MB pack and the learner switches to that course. EC-PACK-23 has two halves: the switch resolves to `not-downloaded` rather than launching a session with failing audio, AND `re-download is explicitly initiated with the size shown` - so the switch starts nothing on ANY link, metered or not. EC-CRS-06's auto-resume applies to a download the learner already began, which is the `auto-resume` trigger, not a course tap.

cases.why: EC-PACK-23: the switch must resolve to not-downloaded, not launch a session with failing audio. The refusal is `needs-explicit-start`, not `metered-needs-confirm`: the switch was never a request, so the link never came into it.

A cellular fixture that auto-resumes a 38 MB download is the falsifier named in the invariant. The refusal is `needs-explicit-start`, not `metered-needs-confirm`: the switch was never a request, so the link never came into it.

On wifi the switch STILL starts nothing: `re-download is explicitly initiated with the size shown`. A silent 38 MB fetch the learner never saw the size of is the other half of EC-PACK-23, and a hotspot the OS failed to flag as metered looks exactly like this case.
Offline: nothing starts, and the request is queued for when a link appears.
A pack that is still fully installed: the switch launches the session and offers nothing at all.

explicitStartCases.why: The learner taps the offer on wifi: this is what actually begins the download.
The learner taps it on cellular and confirms, with the size shown.
EC-CRS-06: a download already under way resumes by itself on an unmetered link.
...but never on a metered one, even with a confirm on record: that confirm belonged to the download the learner was looking at, not to a resume days later in another country.
A session start is not a request for 38 MB either.
